intro: Tavira's great tree is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, an olive classified as a Tree of Public Interest in 1984, with a hollow trunk 7.74 metres round. Portugal's forest service registers its age at more than two thousand years, a figure nobody has tested. It stands in the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia, a few kilometres southwest of the town, and Tavira's own tourist route sends visitors to it.
meta_description: The Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei near Tavira, an olive classified in 1984 with a hollow trunk 7.74 metres round.
question_meta: Tavira's mapped tree is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, a classified olive at Santa Luzia that its register calls about two thousand years old.
question_answer: The tree mapped in Tavira is the Oliveira Real of Pedras d'el Rei, an olive at Santa Luzia classified as a Tree of Public Interest in 1984. Portugal's forest service measured its trunk at 7.74 metres round in 2006 and gave it an age of 2,210 years, a claim nobody has dated.
question_context: The Oliveira Real is on the national register of Trees of Public Interest kept by the ICNF, Portugal's forest service, classified on 2 August 1984. Its 2006 measurement gives 10.3 metres of height and a trunk 7.74 metres round; a 2007 visit by tree bloggers measured 7.8 metres, and the Tree of the Year nomination quotes 11 metres of perimeter, probably taken lower down. The age of 2,210 years is the register's figure and the nomination repeats it, but no ring count or published dating study supports it, so read it as somewhere between one and two thousand years. It was a candidate for Portugal's Tree of the Year in 2022. The trunk is hollow, split into several limbs. It stands on the Rua Jorge Amado inside the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia; Tavira municipality's route 'Os segredos e encantos da Ria Formosa' tells visitors to pass the reception, take the second street on the left and look left after about 25 metres. A second large olive, unclassified, grows nearby.

trees.story:
Tavira's own tourist route sends you past a holiday resort's reception desk to see this olive. Portugal classified it a Tree of Public Interest in 1984, and when the forest service measured it in 2006 the trunk was 7.74 metres round and the tree 10.3 metres tall. The register gave it an age of 2,210 years.

Read that number as a claim. The register and the 2021 Tree of the Year nomination both put it near two thousand years, and tree bloggers who visited in 2007 repeated a carbon-dating figure of about 2,000 without saying who did the dating. No ring count or published study has turned up. Somewhere between one and two thousand years is the honest version, and even the low end makes it older than the kingdom of Portugal.

The trunk is hollow and split into separate limbs, with a gap between two of them wide enough to look inside. Nominated for Portugal's Tree of the Year in 2022, it stands among the low white houses of the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village at Santa Luzia, a few kilometres southwest of Tavira. The municipal route gives the directions. Pass the reception, take the second street on the left, the Rua Jorge Amado, and it is about 25 metres along on the left. A second large olive grows nearby, unclassified and unmeasured since a 2007 visit put it near six metres round.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the hollow trunk, 7.74 metres round and split into several limbs. It stands about 25 metres along the Rua Jorge Amado, on the left, the second street left after the resort reception.

official_register.name: ICNF Arvoredo de Interesse Publico KNJ1/195

trees.access: Inside the Pedras d'el Rei holiday village (aldeamento turistico) at Santa Luzia. Tavira municipality's own route 'Os segredos e encantos da Ria Formosa' sends visitors past the resort reception to the tree on the Rua Jorge Amado; no fee is mentioned.
trees.transport: A few kilometres southwest of Tavira's centre by road, past Santa Luzia; the municipal route reaches it by car on the CM1347.
